content.Abstract: This new teaching dossier rehearses a bounded diagnosis-and-repair report using synthetic hazard-avoidance records.
content.Problem and contribution: The study structure separates stage diagnosis, deployable repair and diagnostic oracle evidence.
content.Methods: A frozen task matrix, episode pair key, seed list, success rule and analysis plan are attached to the locked evaluator version.
content.Results: The synthetic repair did not meet the teaching minimum-improvement criterion; denominator, interval and missing-pair boundaries are retained.
content.Related work: VLA-Arena organizes evaluation across levels and suites, while open VLA work motivates policy evaluation. The dossier contributes a claim-evidence workflow, not a competing model.
content.Limitations: This simulator exercise uses a narrow task suite, has no formal checkpoint, carries large statistical uncertainty, and cannot generalize to a physical robot or unseen embodiment.
content.Ethics and safety: Reported safety is not a deployment certificate. Misuse through inflated claims is a risk; resource and carbon-relevant run totals should be disclosed; license obligations govern redistribution; privacy review is required before collecting real workspace video.
content.Negative results: The negative result and inconclusive interval are preserved; not equivalence is the required interpretation, and the stopping rule forbids opportunistic expansion.
content.Reproducibility: The synthetic dossier includes version hashes, immutable inputs, generators and machine checkers.
content.Conclusion: The bounded outcome is no demonstrated improvement in this fixture; no real-model conclusion follows.
